record.title: GUI burst controls (snapshot, stray stop, gui_changes) are skipped after a sandbox restore and dropped while the sandbox is paused
record.description: GUI input (click/type/key) bypasses the exec approval gate by design (N-1, documented in README.md and run-2 N-1-OPTIONS.md). The partial mitigation is per-burst state held in service memory (_gui_burst, _gui_input_at, _gui_snap_at): a snapshot, a /workspace manifest and baseline pids when a burst opens, then on close a stop of the uid-1001 processes started during the burst and a gui_changes audit record. Two human lifecycle actions leave that state inconsistent with the container; both were reproduced through the real routes (agentbox.api.build) against the real AgentBox/SandboxManager code, with a fake Docker SDK and a virtual clock. (1) Restore: api.py:192 and web.py:243 call end_desktop, which closes the old burst but clears _gui_input_at only when a human lease existed (service.py:494) and never clears _gui_snap_at. If the agent's last GUI input is less than gui_snapshot_idle (60 s) old and the last GUI snapshot less than gui_snapshot_interval (600 s) old, _gui_needs_snapshot returns False, so the first post-restore input takes no snapshot and opens no burst. A uid-1001 background loop the agent starts, and files it edits, in that window are recorded in the next burst's baseline: gui_strays skips the loop (sandbox.py:216) and gui_changes never reports the edits. Clicking every 50 s keeps the window open until the 600 s interval expires. A human takeover before the restore (handback clears _gui_input_at) or a burst that had already idled out removes the gap (negative controls). (2) Pause: the pause route (api.py:166-170; JSON API only, no UI or CLI control) does no burst handling. Once the open burst's 60 s idle window has passed while the sandbox is paused, the next close_idle_gui_bursts() call pops the burst first (service.py:232); desktop_processes then fails in _require_running (sandbox.py:469) and the manifest read fails (Docker refuses exec in a paused container), and both failures are swallowed (service.py:221-222, 238-239). Strays are not stopped and nothing is logged; after resume the loop is still running and is absorbed into the next baseline. No human UI is needed for the trigger: every agent tool call starts with close_idle_gui_bursts() (service.py:273), and an agent screenshot call on the paused sandbox (HTTP 400) was enough. Net effect: a prompt-injected agent can keep a persistent, unlogged uid-1001 background process inside its own sandbox that the documented burst controls are meant to stop. No privilege, container-boundary or cross-sandbox effect was shown, and the typed commands stay in the audit log (tool_request args). The architecture summary names no comparable baseline, so none was used for calibration.
record.root_cause: Burst bookkeeping (_gui_burst, _gui_input_at, _gui_snap_at) is in-memory, keyed only by sandbox id, and is not reconciled with container lifecycle transitions. end_desktop (service.py:529-537) closes the burst but leaves the timers that _gui_needs_snapshot (service.py:186-197) uses to decide whether a burst is already running, so the first input after a restore is treated as a continuation of a burst that no longer exists. _close_gui_burst (service.py:229-239) discards the burst before its enforcement steps, and _stop_gui_strays and the manifest read swallow every exception (service.py:221-222, 238-239), so when close_idle_gui_bursts (service.py:250-256) runs against a paused sandbox the burst is lost without stopping strays or logging changes; the pause route (api.py:166-170) neither closes nor protects the burst.
record.intended_behavior: A burst belongs to one container generation and one running period. The first GUI input after a restore or resume opens a fresh burst (snapshot, manifest, baseline pids), as it already does after a human handback (service.py:494), and a burst is discarded only after its strays have been stopped and its changes logged: it is closed while the container still runs (before pausing or restoring) or kept until the sandbox runs again. Enforcement failures should be recorded, not swallowed.

trace.description: Lower-trust entrypoint: the per-sandbox agent token (principal, api.py:92-101) can call click/type/key on its desktop sandbox, which the default policy allows without approval; each call runs AgentBox.call_tool.
Every GUI input stamps _gui_input_at before it executes (even if it then fails); _gui_snap_at is stamped in _snapshot (service.py:263) and is never cleared anywhere.

trace.scope: POST /sandboxes/{sid}/restore (human token; the Web UI route web.py:243 calls the same end_desktop and the CLI restore command posts to this route)
trace.description: Human restore calls box.end_desktop(sid, 'sandbox_restored') and then sandboxes.restore, which removes the old container and starts a new one (sandbox.py:513-517).
Closes the old burst (logging changes up to the restore) but clears _gui_input_at only through handback when a lease exists (service.py:494) and never clears _gui_snap_at.
With the last input under 60 s and the last snapshot under 600 s old this returns False regardless of container generation, so the first post-restore GUI input takes no snapshot and opens no burst.
The next burst records every current pid as its baseline, including uid-1001 processes started in the burst-less window.
Logs and pauses the container; the open burst is neither closed nor kept safe.

Closes any burst whose last input is older than 60 s regardless of sandbox status; runs at the start of every call_tool (service.py:273) and from expire_stale (373), GET /audit (api.py:258) and the /ui/audit poll (web.py:261).
Pops the burst before the stray stop and the manifest diff run, so a failure in either loses the burst for good.
Raises SandboxError for a paused sandbox; workspace_manifest (sandbox.py:498) has no such guard and relies on Docker refusing exec in a paused container.
'except Exception: return' swallows the paused-sandbox failure: no kill and no gui_processes_stopped; the manifest failure at service.py:238-239 likewise skips gui_changes.
Baseline pids are skipped, so a loop started in the burst-less window or in a dropped burst is never stopped and keeps running outside any burst.

evidence.description: _gui_input_at is popped only in _handback_locked, i.e. when a human lease existed; _gui_snap_at is never popped anywhere (declared 70, read 195, written 263).
The input timer is stamped before the GUI call runs, so calls that fail during a restore or on a paused sandbox still refresh it.
last_input and last_snap are looked up by sandbox id only; nothing ties them to a container generation or running state.
Pause route only logs (168) and pauses (169); there is no burst handling, and pause/resume appear nowhere in tests/.
Every call_tool, including an agent call against a paused sandbox, begins with close_idle_gui_bursts().
/ui/audit (polled every 3 s by templates/sandbox.html:19) runs close_idle_gui_bursts(); /ui/notify and the approvals fragments do so through expire_stale (service.py:373).
_require_running raises for a paused sandbox; _desktop (680) uses it, so desktop_processes (688) and kill_processes (697) fail while paused.
workspace_manifest uses _container() without a paused check; it only fails because Docker refuses exec in a paused container (modelled, not observed).
A failed manifest read returns silently after the burst was already popped, so no gui_changes record is written.
Only restore with an open burst is tested (closing and logging before the restore); there is no test for GUI input after a restore or for a burst idling out while paused.
Documents the promise at lines 197-200: snapshot at burst start, gui_changes and background-process stop at burst end; the restore gap and the paused-burst drop silently void it.

conditions.description: Agent token (agt_...) of a desktop-template sandbox; click/type/key are default-allowed by default_policy.yaml (default: allow). No other privilege is needed.

Restore variant: a human restores a snapshot (Web UI, CLI restore or POST /sandboxes/{id}/restore) without first taking over the screen, and the agent then starts a uid-1001 background process (for example from a GUI terminal) before its next burst opens.

Pause variant: a human pauses the sandbox with POST /sandboxes/{id}/pause (JSON API only; there is no UI or CLI control) while a burst is open, and the pause outlasts the 60 s idle window; any later close_idle_gui_bursts() trigger (the agent's own tool call, GET /audit, the UI polls) then drops the burst.

The restore must land less than 60 s after the agent's last GUI input and less than 600 s after the last GUI snapshot. The burst-less window then ends at the first input pause longer than 60 s or when the last GUI snapshot is older than 600 s.
GUI burst mechanism enabled (AGENTBOX_GUI_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL > 0, default 600; AGENTBOX_GUI_SNAPSHOT_IDLE default 60) on a desktop template.

The gui_changes half of the pause variant relies on the Docker daemon refusing 'docker exec' in a paused container (HTTP 409); the stray-stop half does not (source-visible _require_running). The sandbox has no Docker socket, so the refusal is modelled rather than observed.

execution.attacker_perspective: A prompt-injected agent holding only its sandbox's agent token drives click/type/key on a desktop sandbox. It keeps issuing GUI input at most 60 s apart so its burst timers stay fresh across a human restore, then starts a uid-1001 background loop from a GUI terminal and edits /workspace files in the burst-less window. For the pause case the loop is started before the freeze, and the agent can fire the final trigger itself with any tool call after the burst's 60 s idle window.
payloads: control: agent POST /sandboxes/{sid}/tools/click (t=0; opens burst + snapshot); GUI effect: terminal, bash and a setsid loop started, report.md edited; human GET /audit at t=61 -> idle close stops the shell and the loop and logs gui_processes_stopped + gui_changes

restore: agent click (t=0); human POST /sandboxes/{sid}/restore {snapshot_id: <t=0 snapshot>} (t=10); agent click (t=20) -> no snapshot, no burst; GUI effect in that window: terminal, bash, setsid loop, report.md edited; agent type after 61 s of idle (t=81) opens the next burst; human GET /audit (t=142) -> idle close stops nothing and logs nothing

restore (hunter's shape): as above, then agent click every 50 s from t=70 to t=570 (no snapshot, no burst), click at t=610 -> snapshot because the 600 s interval is exceeded, baseline includes the loop; GET /audit at t=671 -> nothing stopped, nothing logged

pause: agent click (t=0); GUI effect: terminal, bash, setsid loop, report.md edited; agent click (t=10); human POST /sandboxes/{sid}/pause (t=15); at t=95 either human GET /audit or agent POST /sandboxes/{sid}/tools/screenshot (HTTP 400) -> burst dropped; human POST /sandboxes/{sid}/resume (t=105); agent click (t=205) -> new burst whose baseline contains the loop; human GET /audit (t=266) -> nothing stopped, nothing logged
instructions: Inside the approved sandbox run: sbx v12 /usr/bin/python3.13 -I /scratch/v12_harness.py [source-tree] (no network, no Docker socket, read-only /target, uid 65534). The harness builds the real FastAPI app with agentbox.api.build(): real AgentBox, AuditLog, ApprovalStore, Policy (default_policy.yaml), DesktopControl and the real SandboxManager. Only docker.from_env() is replaced by an in-memory fake of the Docker SDK surface (containers.run/get, exec_run, commit, pause/unpause, remove, images.get); jinja2 (absent there) is stubbed and agentbox.service.time is replaced by a virtual clock.

Modelled Docker behaviour, the only assumption not visible in source: exec into a paused container fails with HTTP 409 (APIError); docker commit copies the file layer and docker run from the snapshot image starts a fresh process table; kill -KILL as uid 1001 removes only uid-1001 processes. GUI side effects (terminal window, bash, a setsid loop as uid 1001, an edit of report.md) are applied to the fake container at the step where the agent's keystrokes would have produced them.

Drive each sequence through the real routes with a Starlette TestClient: agent token for POST /sandboxes/{sid}/tools/click|type|screenshot; human token for POST /sandboxes, /restore, /pause, /resume and GET /audit (plus a cookie session and POST /desktop/takeover for the takeover negative control). Dummy sandbox, dummy tokens and a dummy report.md only.

Run the control, the restore variant (idle-gap form and the 50-second-click form), the restore negative controls (burst already idle-closed; human takeover before the restore), the pause variant (human audit poll, and agent screenshot as the dropping call) and an early-resume control; record snapshots, kills, baselines and gui_* events.

Re-run the same file with /scratch/patched (a copy of agentbox/ with agents/v12/artifacts/v12_fix.diff applied) to check the proposed fix. Artifacts: agents/v12/artifacts/v12_harness.py, v12_burst.out (unmodified target), v12_burst_patched.out (patched copy), v12_fix.diff.
execution.observed_result: Unmodified target. Control (no lifecycle event): click opens a burst with a snapshot; the idle close stops pids 102 (bash) and 110 (setsid loop) and logs gui_processes_stopped and gui_changes (modified report.md). Restore: the timers survive the human restore (gui_input_at and gui_snap_at unchanged); the first post-restore click at t=20 takes no snapshot and opens no burst; the loop (pid 110) and the report.md edit made in that window land in the next burst's baseline [.., 100, 102, 110]; after that burst's idle close kills=[], the loop is still running and there is no gui_processes_stopped or gui_changes event. The 50-second-click form behaves the same (12 clicks, still one snapshot; the click at t=610 snapshots and baselines the loop; nothing stopped or logged). Negative controls: a burst that had idle-closed before the restore, and a human takeover before the restore (handback pops _gui_input_at), both snapshot on the first post-restore click and then stop the loop and log gui_changes as designed. Pause: the human pause leaves the burst open; the human audit poll (or the agent's own screenshot call, HTTP 400) at t=95 drops it (burst_open=false) with kills=[], one refused exec on the paused container and no gui_* events; after resume the loop is still running, the next burst's baseline includes pids 100, 102, 110 and its idle close again stops nothing and logs nothing. Early-resume control: the burst survives the short pause and closes normally (loop stopped, gui_changes logged). Patched copy: all eight scenarios behave like the control (restore: first post-restore click snapshots and opens a burst, loop stopped, gui_changes logged; pause: burst closed before the freeze with reason sandbox_paused, loop stopped, gui_changes logged).

remediation.strategy: Treat container lifecycle transitions as burst boundaries. (1) After closing the burst in end_desktop (restore and delete), clear _gui_input_at and _gui_snap_at so the first GUI input after a restore always snapshots and opens a fresh burst; optionally reset once more after the container swap so a GUI call in flight during the swap cannot re-arm the timers or leave a stale burst. (2) Close the burst while the container still runs when pausing (call a new end_gui_burst from the pause route before sandboxes.pause) and clear the timers so the first input after resume opens a new burst. (3) Never discard a burst when enforcement cannot run: skip paused sandboxes in close_idle_gui_bursts and _gui_needs_snapshot (or re-insert the burst when the stray stop or manifest read fails and the sandbox still exists), and write an audit event when enforcement fails instead of swallowing the exception. (4) Add regression tests for a GUI input right after a restore with fresh timers and for a burst whose idle window ends while the sandbox is paused. The change in the code_changes entries was applied to a scratch copy and made all eight harness scenarios behave like the control.

likelihood.reason: Needs a prompt-injected agent that uses the default-allowed desktop GUI tools plus a human lifecycle action the agent cannot cause: a restore without a prior takeover within 60 s of the agent's last GUI input, or a pause (JSON API only) that outlasts the 60 s idle window. A takeover/handback or an already idle-closed burst removes the restore gap (verified). Once the human has acted, the agent only has to keep issuing inputs and start a background process, and for pause the agent can fire the final trigger itself.

impact.reason: Only the best-effort compensating controls of the documented, accepted N-1 GUI bypass are lost: a uid-1001 background process started in the window is never stopped and /workspace changes made in it are never diffed into gui_changes. The agent can already run arbitrary uid-1001 code through the GUI; container isolation (network none, dropped capabilities) is untouched, no privilege or cross-sandbox effect was shown, the snapshot that was just restored stays available as a recovery point, and the typed commands remain visible in the audit log. The harness shows loss of the control outputs, not what the surviving process then does.

confidence.reason: The restore variant is pure state logic, reproduced through the real HTTP routes with the real AgentBox, SandboxManager, AuditLog and DesktopControl, with negative controls (takeover, idle-closed burst, early resume) and a patched-copy run in which every scenario behaves like the control. The pause variant's stray-stop failure follows from _require_running (source-certain); its gui_changes half depends on Docker refusing exec in a paused container, which is modelled in the harness but cannot be observed in the sandbox (no Docker socket).
